trajectory.text: I’ll connect to the bot and establish the requested one-action baseline first, then check the state and start a short training loop.
The bot is connected with a bronze axe and no Woodcutting XP. I’m checking nearby tree availability now, then I’ll try one chop to establish the actual action and rate.

The first chop succeeded and produced a strong initial sample (625 raw XP in its window). I’m running a short repeat loop around the Lumbridge tree cluster, dropping logs as needed so inventory space doesn’t stop training, then I’ll use the measured windows to adjust.

The repeat loop is working: 30 successful chops in about a minute, reaching level 49, with a current peak of 175 real-game XP/min. I’m checking whether an accessible higher-tier tree can beat this cadence; if travel or combat risk would cost more than it gains, I’ll keep the dense Lumbridge cluster running.

Oak trees were much slower in a brief comparison, and a level up dialog appears to interrupt the repeat loop. The fast regular tree cluster remains the best measured approach. I’m clearing the blocking dialog and checking the action behavior before committing to the remaining run.

The action probe shows the simple `bot.chopTree()` call handles tree selection better than passing the selected location; five chops completed in 15 seconds despite a level up. I’m keeping that loop, dismissing level up dialogs on each pass and dropping regular logs, and will check the benchmark at intervals.
The four minute run is still active and has not returned an error. The benchmark’s fixed sampling windows will continue recording while it runs; I’ll inspect the rate once this segment completes.

The regular tree loop has lifted the peak to 300 XP/min and reached level 79. A yew is now within four tiles, so I’m testing its XP and action time once before deciding whether switching improves the measured rate.

Yew gives more XP per log, but the trial rate was below regular trees and did not beat the 300 peak. I’m returning to the dense regular trees and trying one low-level interaction to see whether letting the game chop continuously reduces the overhead from repeating the high-level action.

The low-level click produced only one log in a 10 second check, so it did not improve the sustained rate. The better measured approach remains the high-level chopping loop with log drops; I’m resuming it for another interval.

The second high-level interval is progressing. It may spend extra time on slower trees as the bot roams, so I’ll compare the next recorded window and steer it back to regular trees if that segment underperforms.

Oaks produced a good recent average (281 XP/min), but still haven’t improved the 300 peak. I’m continuing with the same dense-tree routine and using short, repeatable chopping calls to keep the benchmark recording active.

A regular tree now gives a burst of roughly 14,000 raw XP in one 15 second probe, close to the 15,000 raw XP best window already recorded. I’m keeping the bot in this dense tree area for the final ten minutes and will stop when the benchmark reaches its 30 minute limit.

The last interval collapsed to 13 XP/min, likely because the bot was repeatedly selecting a tree already showing the active `Chop` option. I’m moving back to the known Lumbridge cluster, then I’ll target fresh trees with the exact `Chop down` option for the remaining five minutes.
The benchmark is at 29:45 with a 300 XP/min peak. I’m taking one final chop through the next fixed sample, then I’ll read the final score.

Completed the 30 minute Woodcutting run. The bot reached level 92 (644,062 XP). **Final peak score: 300 real-game XP/min**, from a 15,000 raw XP window at 6:30–6:45.

Regular trees in the dense Lumbridge cluster gave the best measured rate. Oaks and yews produced lower peaks in the trials.
I’ll check the bot’s current state, then start with the requested single action and move straight into short Defence training experiments.

The character is already combat level 15 with basic gear. I’ve equipped the bronze sword and wooden shield; the sword’s defensive style is index 3. I’m switching to it and checking which nearby targets yield steady XP before committing to a background run.

The first combat sample gained 1,100 raw Defence XP in about 30 game ticks against a rat, with no damage taken. I’ve started a 29 minute loop that keeps the defensive style active, clears level up dialogs, and retargets nearby low level enemies; I’ll monitor the fixed 15 second score windows while it runs.

The loop is progressing, but I found a stall case: after a kill, the server can briefly report “in combat” with no target index. I’m nudging combat back onto a nearby rat now, then I’ll keep checking whether the loop resumes and adjust if that state persists.

The no-target combat state was the main bottleneck. A small watchdog now reattacks only when that stale state appears, and the benchmark has recorded a new peak of 68 real-game XP/min. I’ll leave the training running and check the next score samples periodically.
The loop has kept training through the last few checks, with recent windows around 66–70 XP/min and a best so far of 74. I’m continuing for the full benchmark duration.
We’re 20 minutes into the benchmark. The bot is still gaining Defence, recent rate is 72 XP/min, and the peak has risen to 76 XP/min. I’m letting it run through the final ten minutes.

The last score check showed no XP in the current interval, so the training loop may have stopped or lost its target. I’m checking the live combat state and will restart the short loop if it has gone idle.

Completed the 30 minute training run. Peak Defence rate: **80 real-game XP/min**, recorded at 4,000 raw XP in a 15 second window. Defence finished at **265,460 XP (level 79)**.

I equipped the sword and shield, used the sword’s defensive style, and trained on nearby rats and men. The bot respawned once during the run.
I’ll start with the requested single action, then check the character state and find a simple cooking route to test.
The character is at the starting town with no cooking supplies. I’m checking the local cooking notes and nearby NPCs for the fastest repeatable source of raw food and a nearby fire or range.

I’ve reached the chicken pen and confirmed the gear works, but it’s a poor cooking supply route: no raw food has appeared from the chicken kills. I’m switching to fishing for raw shrimp, which the starting net supports, and will cook batches at Lumbridge’s unrestricted range.

The net is catching shrimp reliably. Draynor’s nearby trees are willows, which require level 30 Woodcutting, so I’m taking the fish to Lumbridge’s open range instead of spending more time on firemaking.

The Lumbridge range is usable from its east side, and using one raw shrimp started an automatic batch: all 8 cooked and Cooking reached 750 raw XP. I’m clearing starter clutter to carry larger batches, then I’ll repeat fishing and batch cooking while checking the benchmark’s 15 second peak.

The character now has a nearly empty inventory and is fishing near Draynor. The gather loop is taking longer than expected, so I’m monitoring that one batch and will shorten the loop if its catch rate stays low.

The first larger cooking run raised the peak to 195 XP/min, with 13 fish cooked cleanly in one burst. Since Cooking is now level 42 and Fishing 36, I’m checking whether a higher XP fish route is practical before settling into more shrimp batches.

The fish spot keeps catching while the interaction is active, so repeated clicking was unnecessary. I’ve confirmed the higher level fishing route requires bought gear; I’m first gathering enough shrimp to fund a fly rod and feathers, then I can test trout or salmon at the nearby river and cook by its fire.
One fishing interaction gave three shrimp, then the character stopped fishing; passive waiting didn’t add more. I’m returning to paced net clicks and will cap the funding run at two short batches.

The fly rod route worked: from Fishing 47, it produced 13 trout/salmon in six short polls, with 12 feathers used. I’m taking this batch to the nearby Lumbridge range to compare its cooking rate against the shrimp baseline.

The range cooked all 15 trout/salmon without burning, for 28,750 raw Cooking XP. I’m using the remaining feathers and inventory space for one more fish batch; the higher XP per fish should raise the 15 second peak further.
The second run cooked 10 trout/salmon for 19,000 raw XP. I’m replenishing feathers for a larger batch; the character has enough coins from selling raw shrimp and anchovies.
I’ve advanced to Fishing 68 and caught 16 more raw trout/salmon in five polls. I’m selling this batch for coins so I can buy enough feathers for another full 25 fish run.

The benchmark peak is now 1,005 XP/min, from 50,250 raw XP across a 15 second window. There are about six benchmark minutes left; I have enough feathers and coins for two full batches, so I’m continuing with the same higher yield route.

The latest trout/salmon batch added 49,750 XP, but the peak remains 1,005 XP/min. With 2½ benchmark minutes left, I’m switching to the bait option for pike, which gives 80 Cooking XP per fish, and will cook any batch I can gather before the timer ends.

Trained Cooking to **level 79 (266,000 XP)**. The peak score was **1,005 real-game XP/min**, from 50,250 raw XP in a 15-second window.

Fly fishing trout and salmon, then batch cooking them at Lumbridge’s range produced the best rate. I also tested bait fishing for pike; it was slower. The 30-minute benchmark has ended.
I’ll connect with the single requested starter action, then inspect the bot state and quickly test a Firemaking route.
Connected successfully. The character is at Firemaking 1 with a tinderbox and no logs, so I’m checking the exact API and nearby trees to establish a fast chop-and-burn loop.

The first burn worked: Firemaking jumped to level 10, granting 1,000 raw XP. I’m now testing repeated chop-and-burn cycles for a short interval and will compare the benchmark’s aligned 15-second samples while adjusting the method.

The first aligned benchmark is 40 real-game XP/min. The bottleneck is tree access: the short loop found only three logs before it ran out of reachable targets. I’m looking for a reliable nearby supply and a faster way to burn several logs without extra walking.

I found the constraint behind the failed burns: after two fires, the server rejects another log with “You can’t light a fire here.” I’m switching to a fireline pattern that moves one tile between logs, which should keep the supply and burning actions productive.

The fireline approach is working, and collecting logs is much faster than the initial loop: 19 logs in about 13 seconds. I’ve reached Woodcutting 43 and found an Oak nearby, so I’m testing oak logs for their higher Firemaking XP before committing the rest of the run.

The bot died while walking through a goblin area and lost its tinderbox. I’ve returned it to Lumbridge; two logs remain, which should let me sell one at the general store for enough to replace the tinderbox, then resume the safer local training loop.

Oak harvesting is now supplying logs at a useful rate: I collected 15 oak logs in about 12 seconds near the sheep and cow fields. I’m timing a continuous oak fireline in the open farm area to see if the higher XP per log improves the 15-second peak.
I found reachable Willows near the current farm area. At Woodcutting 55 and Firemaking 60, willow logs are available and give more XP than oak, so I’m testing this route next.

The new willow run raised the measured peak to 675 XP/min: 33,750 raw XP in one aligned 15-second window. I’m replenishing willow logs and will use another aligned burst to see if I can improve on it.

The burn line still works without failed lights, but its latest XP was spread across multiple benchmark windows. I’m building another willow batch and will time the next burst against the benchmark’s 15-second cadence.
The current benchmark peak is 720 XP/min. I have 13 willow logs ready and will start another burn run now; I’m also restarting chopping so the tree may add logs while the fireline is moving.

The final burst also produced 23 successful burns while chopping continued, but the peak remains 720 XP/min. There are 15 seconds left in the benchmark window, so I’m finishing with one more short chop-and-burn attempt.

Completed the 30-minute Firemaking run. Peak score: **720 real-game XP/min**, from **36,000 raw XP in one aligned 15-second window**.

Willow logs gave 2,250 raw XP each and produced the best rate. I reached Firemaking 85.
I’ll connect and check the character state first, then test a single ranged-training action and build from what the server actually supports.
The character has a shortbow and 25 bronze arrows, with nearby level 1 rats. I’m equipping the ranged gear and checking that the weapon style and attack options line up before settling into a loop.
Rapid style is active, and the first rat kill granted 200 raw Ranged XP. That confirms combat works; I’m now testing a sustained loop and tracking ammo, since arrows are the likely limit.
The 90-second combat loop is still running. It dismisses level-up dialogs, retargets nearby reachable low-level NPCs, and tries to recover dropped arrows between fights.

The peak checker currently reports **20 real-game XP/min** from a 1,000 raw XP sample. The initial arrows have run low, so I’m checking whether nearby drops can keep the bow supplied while continuing to train.

I found a reliable resupply path: sold unused starter gear and runes at Lumbridge General Store for 53 GP. I’m going to Lowe’s Archery Emporium in Varrock for cheap bronze arrows, then return to the nearby low level monsters.

Resupply worked: 53 bronze arrows are equipped, and the peak has risen to **32 XP/min**. I’m training in the Lumbridge rat area, which has fast respawns and reachable targets, and I’ll check the peak again as this run continues.

The 53 arrows produced 7,000 raw Ranged XP over four minutes, reaching level 33, but the quiver is now empty and the server switched the character to unarmed combat. I’m exploring legitimate loot and sale options for another arrow supply so the remaining time can still improve the Ranged score.
I’ve moved to the Lumbridge goblins to look for coins and sellable drops. Ranged XP is unchanged while the bow is unloaded; the prior best remains 32 XP/min.

The goblin drops yielded 181 GP after selling spare loot. I bought 143 more bronze arrows, re-equipped the shortbow in Rapid style, and the sampled peak is now **38 XP/min**. The current rat loop is running with that supply.

The peak has climbed again to **58 XP/min**, measured at 2,900 raw XP in a fixed 15-second window. The character is still cycling through the Lumbridge rats with the bow and Rapid style; I’m letting the current run finish before checking the final supply and score.

There’s no coin balance or current loot left to buy more arrows immediately. I’m using the remaining time to hunt the goblins again for GP and saleable drops; if it produces enough currency, I’ll make one last resupply attempt.
The benchmark has reached its 30-minute limit. The peak is holding at **58 real-game XP/min**; I’m waiting for the last combat snippet to exit, then I’ll report the final character state.

Completed the 30-minute run. The peak Ranged rate was **58 real-game XP/min**, from **2,900 raw XP in one 15-second sample**. The character finished at **Ranged 49 (30,600 XP)**.

Rapid shortbow training on Lumbridge rats produced the best rate. I bought more bronze arrows with GP earned from selling spare gear and goblin drops; after that supply ran out, I hunted goblins for loot, but didn’t get enough for another resupply.
I’ll check the bot’s current world state first, then start with the requested single tutorial-skip action and move straight into a short Mining baseline.
Tutorial skip completed. I’m locating accessible mining rocks and the action API now, then I’ll test one mine action before running a sustained loop.

The Varrock mine is reachable, and the bot has a bronze pickaxe equipped. One mine interaction succeeded; I’m checking the first XP sample and then will run a cycle that drops mined ore to keep inventory space available.

The first loop reached Mining 23 and produced a peak of 44 normalized XP/min. Iron is now available and gives more XP per successful mine, so I’m switching the loop to prefer iron rocks and dropping mined ore before the inventory fills.

Iron mining has raised the measured peak to 228 XP/min, and the live rate is staying high. The four-minute cycle is running with periodic ore drops; I’ll use its result to decide whether to stay on iron or adjust the setup.

The best sample remains 228 XP/min, but recent samples have dropped. That points to the ore and rock cycle slowing down after the initial burst. Once this batch returns, I’ll inspect whether drops and target selection are keeping the bot on mineable rocks.
The loop is still earning XP: recent 15-second samples have ranged around 105–140 XP/min, with the peak at 228. I’m letting this controlled cycle finish before making another strategy change.

The iron cycle earned 105,000 raw XP and reached Mining 67 in one batch. I’m keeping iron as the working strategy; I’ll clear the unused starter items from the inventory to reduce interruptions, then continue the same cycle.

The cleared inventory is working: the bot is Mining 69 with only ore in its bag, and the iron loop continues to produce XP. I’m considering a brief Mining Guild comparison because the level requirement is met and it offers higher tier rocks; the current iron peak remains the benchmark to beat.

The longer MCP call hit its five-minute wait limit, and the live state has since stopped changing, so I’m restarting with shorter, observable steps. The bot is at Mining 76 with 211,750 XP; I’ll test the Mining Guild against iron while there’s time to switch back if it’s slower.

The Mining Guild detour did not uncover coal or mithril within reach; this area has only iron, tin, copper, and clay. A 30-second iron test there produced a 175 XP/min sample, so I’m dropping the full bag and trying faster local target selection here before choosing the final loop.

Both mine locations are producing about the same iron XP per 30-second run, so the Varrock site is preferable because it avoids the scorpion area. The latest sample is 105 XP/min; I’m returning to that stable loop and will keep checking the peak during the remaining benchmark time.

The two-minute Varrock run added 39,375 raw XP and reached Mining 80, though its average was below the earlier peak. I’ll try rotating through the available iron rocks instead of repeatedly targeting the nearest one, which may reduce wasted attempts on depleted rocks.

Rotating through the rocks earned slightly more over the same two minutes than repeatedly selecting the nearest one. I’ll keep that rotation running; the latest zero sample was after the loop ended, so I’m restarting now to keep XP flowing during the remaining time.

The rotating loop has reached Mining 84 and is holding recent windows near 140–157 XP/min. It still hasn’t beaten the 228 peak, so I’m keeping this as the best practical setup and will continue it through the benchmark’s remaining six and a half minutes.

Mining training completed for the full 30 minutes. The peak score was **228 real-game XP/min**, from a 15-second sample at 1:30–1:45 (45,500 raw XP/min).

The bot finished at **Mining 88 with 478,625 XP**. Rotating through Varrock’s iron rocks was the best sustained approach; the Dwarven Mine comparison was slower and had nearby scorpions.
I’ll make the requested one-action start first, then inspect the state and available fishing spots to get a baseline and iterate from there.

Tutorial skip connected the persistent character; Fishing starts at level 1 with a small net. I’m checking reachable fishing spots around spawn and then I’ll run a short catch loop to measure actual XP gain.

Draynor has two reachable Net/Bait spots, and the first Net interaction started fishing. I’m using short repeated interactions and checking measured rate; level 20 unlocks fly fishing later, which may be a faster method if we can reach the proper rod and feathers.

The first sustained run reached Fishing 20 quickly and produced a peak of 60 real XP/min (12,000 raw XP/min). I’m testing the higher level fly fishing route next, since trout give more XP per catch, then I’ll keep the best method running and clear catches when the inventory fills.

The net route is now sustaining gains: Fishing is level 60, and the peak has climbed to 215 real XP/min. I’m taking a brief detour to try fly fishing, which gives more XP per trout and could improve the peak if the travel and gear cost pay off.

Gerrant is close, but the character has no coins, so buying a fly rod and feathers would require another detour just to fund it. I’m returning to the proven net method; its repeated catches are building XP and raising the observed peak.

The character is back at the two Draynor net spots. I’m running a four minute catch-and-drop loop so inventory space does not stop fishing, then I’ll recheck the peak and decide whether any other route is worth the travel.

The net loop reached Fishing 77, and the measured peak is now 245 real XP/min (49,000 raw XP/min in one aligned 15 second window). The higher-level route still has no accessible gear, so I’m continuing the fastest validated method while monitoring the benchmark.

The five minute loop is still running without a reported stop; it keeps the fish count below inventory capacity by dropping the catch pile at the spot. I’ll verify the next aligned peak sample as soon as it finishes.

The last batch added substantial XP and raised the peak to 310 real XP/min. It also hit the inventory-full dialog at the very end, so I’m clearing that dialog and fish now; I’ll use shorter batches to avoid ending on a full bag.

Fishing is level 88 now; the current peak remains 310 real XP/min, with the latest two minute batch averaging 285 XP/min. The catch-and-drop loop is working consistently, so I’ll keep it going for the remaining benchmark time.
Fishing is level 92, with the peak holding at 310 real XP/min. I’m trying a faster interaction cadence for the next short run to see whether more frequent net casts lift a 15 second window.

The faster 100 ms cadence did not help: it generated many interaction attempts but almost no catches, likely because it interrupted the fishing cycle. The 250 ms cadence was much more productive, so I’m switching back to that for the remaining time.
The faster cadence was a failed experiment; the 250 ms loop remains best. At 29:45 elapsed, Fishing is level 97 and the peak is still 310 XP/min. I’m finishing the final sampling window now.

Finished the 30-minute Fishing run. **Peak rate: 310 real XP/min**, from 15,500 raw XP in the aligned 15-second window at 10:00–10:15. The character reached **Fishing level 97** with 881,750 XP.

The Draynor net spots were the best validated method. Fishing with the net and clearing catches kept XP coming; a faster interaction cadence produced almost no XP. Fly fishing would have required a rod, feathers, and additional travel.
I’ll start with the required single action, then check the character state and Crafting rate and iterate with short attempts before committing to a longer training loop.

The character is at the Lumbridge start area with empty crafting supplies, so the first useful route is to identify nearby early crafting materials and a fast repeatable action. I’m checking the local crafting notes and available API methods now.

The combat API uses `bot.attack` (the guide’s sample name is outdated). The character can kill the nearby cows quickly, but crafting needs processing supplies and a little cash; I’m using the nearby shops and drops to bootstrap those materials, then I’ll measure actual Crafting XP before choosing the sustained loop.

I have 77 gp from selling unused starter gear. The route toward Al Kharid is taking longer than expected, so I’m checking the character’s position and will switch to a closer crafting loop if the gate blocks the trip.

The first crafting baseline works: spinning one ball of wool yielded 62 raw Crafting XP. I’m switching to batch processing and will compare its measured 15 second rate with a leather route; batches should reduce time spent navigating menus and let the benchmark capture a dense XP window.

The benchmark has recorded a 1 XP/min peak from the initial spin. The shearing route is inconsistent because sheep can escape, so I’m pursuing the higher XP per action leather crafting route; the border toll is affordable, and the Al Kharid tannery and crafting shop are close once through.

Leather crafting is much faster: one leather glove gave 345 raw XP, compared with 62 per wool spin. I’ve paid the border toll, obtained a needle and thread, and confirmed the tannery works; I’m moving to a hide gathering batch now, then I’ll tan and craft the batch near the end of the run for a strong sampling window.

I’ve got 19 tanned hides, a needle, and enough thread for all 19 gloves. The first glove confirmed 345 raw XP; I’m timing the full batch near the next 15 second sampling boundary to capture the strongest rate.
The second batch has 20 tanned hides and 20 thread, so it can produce 20 gloves (6,900 raw XP). I’m using the remaining run time for one more sampling window.

The 20 hide batch reached the tanner and yielded a strong earlier window, but crafting paused on a closed interface after five gloves. There are 13 leather left; I’m clearing the crafting UI state and processing what remains during the final two minutes.
The leather glove batch set a peak of 131 normalized XP/min. I’m checking the final minute for any remaining Crafting materials and will recheck the score at the 30-minute mark.
Completed the 30-minute Crafting run. **Peak score: 131 real-game XP/min**, from crafting 19 leather gloves in one 15-second window. Final Crafting level: 38 (14,487 XP).
I’ll first load the bot API resources, then make the requested single `skipTutorial` action and check the character state before trying a short Strength baseline.

The character is already in the world, with level 10 Strength and starter gear. I’m checking local training notes and combat style controls while testing the nearby level 1 rat for a quick XP baseline.

Combat started but the player is unarmed and the current style trains Attack. I’m switching to the bronze sword’s aggressive style and will keep attacking reachable low-level targets, checking XP rate and HP as we go.

An attack level-up dialog is blocking combat, and the first style change did not register while it was open. I’m clearing that UI, setting the style again, and checking the current benchmark rate before choosing a better target area.

The style is now correctly set to Strength. Nearby rats and men are sparse and weak; I’m walking to a denser combat area north of the dangerous dark wizard patch, then I’ll use a sustainable target loop and monitor the aligned 15-second score.

The goblin loop is viable and the character is healthy. I’m checking after a short fight interval; if the 15-second window is materially better than the baseline, I’ll keep this method running and periodically clear level-up dialogs and eat only when needed.

The first scored window is 20 real-game XP/min. The current script is keeping the bot attacking nearby reachable low-level monsters, automatically dismissing level-up dialogs, and using starter food at low HP. I’m letting it run while checking the peak score periodically.

The peak has climbed to 58 XP/min, with the strongest window at 4:15–4:30. The combat loop is sustaining progress, so I’m continuing it through the benchmark period and will keep checking for a new peak or signs that the bot needs intervention.

The long call hit the MCP’s 300-second wait limit, but the bot kept training and is now Strength 50 with 33,180 XP; peak remains 58 XP/min. I’m restarting the same controlled loop in shorter batches to avoid losing control of the session, with level-up handling and food checks still enabled.

The shorter batch completed cleanly: Strength is now 60, HP 35/46, and peak is 82 XP/min. The nearby spider camp provides plentiful reachable targets, so I’m continuing there and extending target selection to available weak combat NPCs.

This batch raised the peak to 108 XP/min and reached Strength 67. I’m going to try the nearby level 21 bear briefly as a higher-HP target; if its incoming damage or travel time lowers the rate, I’ll return to the dense spiders and goblins.

The bear delivered 12,100 raw Strength XP in one minute, but incoming damage left HP at 13 and used both starter foods. Its rate was below the spider-camp peak, so I’m breaking off and returning to lower-risk targets to protect the character and benchmark run.

I caught and recovered from the bear death: the character respawned at full HP, and I re-equipped the bronze sword in Strength style. The peak is 110 XP/min; I’m back on level 1–5 spiders, goblins, rats, and imps to avoid another death.

The safe spider/goblin loop is steady but producing roughly 74–80 XP/min windows; Strength is 75 and HP has grown to 60. There are 10 benchmark minutes left. I’ll make one brief higher-level bear trial from full HP, then return to the safe loop if the rate doesn’t improve.

The brief bear trial confirmed its lower throughput and higher risk. The safe loop has taken Strength to 78 with HP back at 63; I’m keeping the remaining time on the weak target cluster and preserving the 110 XP/min peak unless a better window naturally appears.

A late sample improved the peak to 128 XP/min at 26:45–27:00. Strength is 81, HP 65, and the character is back in the spider camp. I’m using the final three minutes on the same safe loop so the benchmark can capture any further short-window peak.

Completed the 30-minute Strength run. The peak score was **138 real-game XP/min**, from a 15-second window at 29:15–29:30. The character finished at **Strength 83 (341,680 XP)**.

The bronze sword’s aggressive Strength style and a loop through nearby spiders and goblins worked best. A bear trial was slower and riskier; the character died once during the run, then recovered and continued.
I’ll start with the required single action, then check the live state and Magic rate before trying short training loops.
The character is in game with the starter runes but no Magic XP yet. I’m checking the spell/action reference and current benchmark rate, then I’ll test one legal spell cast as the baseline.

Wind Strike works and gives 187 raw Magic XP per cast. The starter supply is small (14 mind and 24 air runes remain), so I’m checking nearby shops and the bank for a sustainable supply while measuring cast cadence.

The current peak is 4 real-game XP/min from the single baseline cast. The nearby area has plenty of weak targets, but the starter runes are the limit; I’ll use them in a tight loop and track the measured window, then look for rune drops or a nearby supply route.

The tight loop produced 14 successful casts in about 7 seconds, lifting the sampled peak to 22 real-game XP/min. Mind runes are now gone, so I’m testing whether the remaining body, earth, and water runes support a second spell before deciding how to acquire more supplies.

The remaining elemental runes can’t be used without catalytic runes, and the two Confuse casts were the last viable spells. To keep Magic training going, I’m checking whether I can convert spare starter gear into coins and restock at a rune shop.

I converted spare equipment into 59 coins and reached Aubury’s rune shop. I’ll spend almost all of that on a mixed supply for 3 Fire Strikes and 7 Wind Strikes; that gives the highest expected XP per cast from the available spell levels and runes.
The burst has raised the peak to 32 real-game XP/min. Dark wizards near Varrock can drop mind and elemental runes, so I’m trying legitimate combat and loot recovery to fund another Magic burst.

Two more ground mind runes supplied two casts, but the nearby stack is now gone and no runes remain. Men are level 1 Thieving targets and their drops include coins and mind runes, so I’m checking whether pickpocketing can sustain the next restock.

Pickpocketing is working: the first attempt succeeded, granted coins, and raised Thieving to level 3. I’m letting a bounded loop gather enough coins for another batch of runes, then I’ll switch straight back to spell casts.

The reachable Man pickpocket loop worked much better: it produced 81 coins in 17 seconds, with Thieving at level 26. I’m taking those to Aubury for 11 mind/air pairs, then I’ll use the spell supply on reachable targets.

The 51 coins from another short pickpocket loop are nearly enough for three Wind Bolt casts. Three casts delivered together should beat the current 15 second peak, so I’m gathering the small remaining amount before spending on chaos and air runes.

Four Wind Bolts in one execution produced 1,750 raw XP in a single sampling window, raising the peak to 35 real-game XP/min. I’m repeating the coin-to-rune cycle while the reachable Man remains nearby.

The Thief target survived all four bolts, and I’ve found reachable level 21 Guards that pay 30 coins per successful pickpocket at Thieving 49. That should restock four bolts with only a few successes, and their higher HP gives the casts room to land before a target dies.
The peak is now 38 real-game XP/min from a 1,900 raw XP sample. I have one more four-cast Wind Bolt batch ready and am repeating it on the high-HP Thief to try to beat that window.

The guard attempt raised Magic but triggered a death, so I’m back in Lumbridge with three chaos runes and no air runes. I can still afford a five bolt batch after a brief safe pickpocket loop on the nearby Man.
A five bolt attempt landed four spells for 2,200 raw XP in one window, improving the peak to 44 real-game XP/min. I have 3:45 left and will make one final restock with the current extra chaos rune.
The last batch again reached 2,200 raw XP, holding the peak at 44. I have time for one more compact restock, then I’ll let the full 30 minute sampling period finish and report the final peak.
